months.1:
# Muharram (Sacred Month)

The first month of the Islamic calendar and one of the four Sacred Months.

> The Prophet (ﷺ) called it "The Month of Allah" (Shahr Allah).

**Recommended Acts:**  
- Fasting: "The best fasting after the month of Ramadan is the month of Allah, Al-Muharram." (Sahih Muslim)
- Ashura: Fasting on the 10th of Muharram expiates the sins of the previous year.
months.2:
# Safar

Safar is the second month of the Hijri calendar. Historically, it was a time when Arabs would leave their homes for travel or war, leaving them empty (sifr).

**Correction of Beliefs:**  
The Prophet (ﷺ) negated pre-Islamic superstitions associated with Safar, stating: "There is no bad omens... and no [evil omen in] Safar." (Sahih Bukhari). This teaches us to place full trust in Allah alone.
months.3:
# Rabi al-Awwal

The month of the birth of the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). The name translates to "The First Spring."

**Significance:**  
This month is cherished for the arrival of the final Messenger who brought the light of Islam to humanity. It is a time to renew our connection with his Sunnah and study his life (Seerah).
months.4:
# Rabi al-Thani

The fourth month of the Islamic calendar, meaning "The Second Spring."

**Reflection:**  
As proper seasons change, so do the seasons of life. It serves as a continuity of the time for growth and learning established in the previous month.
months.5:
# Jumada al-Awwal

The fifth month, denoting the beginning of the dry/parched season in pre-Islamic Arabia.

**Historical Event:**  
The Battle of Mu'tah took place in this month (8 AH), where great companions like Zaid bin Harithah, Ja'far bin Abi Talib, and Abdullah bin Rawahah (RA) were martyred. It reminds us of the sacrifices made for the faith.
months.6:
# Jumada al-Akhirah

The sixth month of the Islamic calendar.

**Historical Event:**  
The Battle of Yarmouk, a major victory for Muslims under the Caliphate of Umar (RA), occurred in this month. It is also the month in which the beloved daughter of the Prophet (ﷺ), Fatimah (RA), passed away.
months.7:
# Rajab (Sacred Month)

Rajab is the seventh month and one of the four Sacred Months in which fighting is prohibited and good deeds are magnified.

**Key Event:**  
**Isra and Mi'raj:** The miraculous Night Journey and Ascension of the Prophet (ﷺ) took place on the 27th of Rajab, gifting the Ummah with the five daily prayers.
months.8:
# Sha'ban

The month preceding Ramadan. The Prophet (ﷺ) used to fast most of this month.

**Virtue:**  
It is the month in which deeds are raised to the Lord of the worlds. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I love that my deeds be raised while I am fasting."

**Mid-Sha'ban:** The 15th night is a night of forgiveness (Shab-e-Barat).
months.9:
# Ramadan (The Blessed Month)

The ninth month, in which the Quran was revealed. It is the month of obligatory fasting, Taraweeh prayers, and immense charity.

> "The month of Ramadan [is that] in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for the people..." (Quran 2:185)

It contains **Laylat al-Qadr**, a night better than a thousand months.
months.10:
# Shawwal

The month of Eid al-Fitr and the reward of a lifetime of fasting.

**Virtue:**  
Fasting six days in Shawwal after Ramadan yields the reward of fasting for the entire year.

> The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever fasts Ramadan then follows it with six days of Shawwal, it is as if he fasted for a lifetime." (Sahih Muslim)
months.11:
# Dhul Qadah (Sacred Month)

The eleventh month and the first of the sacred months of Hajj. It is a time of preparation for the pilgrimage.

**Significance:**  
Historically, sitting (Qa'dah) from war to allow safe passage for pilgrims. It is a time to respect the sanctity of peace and prepare for spiritual journeys.
months.12:
# Dhul Hijjah (Sacred Month)

The month of Hajj. The first ten days are the best days of the year.

> The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There are no days in which righteous deeds are more beloved to Allah than these ten days."

**Key Events:**  
- **Day of Arafah (9th):** The pinnacle of Hajj.
- **Eid al-Adha (10th):** The Festival of Sacrifice.

events.new-year:
# Islamic New Year (1st Muharram)

The Islamic New Year marks the beginning of the Hijri calendar, commemorating the Hijrah (migration) of Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and his companions from Mecca to Medina. This event was a turning point in Islamic history, leading to the establishment of the first Muslim community.

While there are no specific prescribed acts of worship for the new year itself, it is a time for reflection on the passage of time and the legacy of the Hijrah.

> "Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve [lunar] months in the register of Allah [from] the day He created the heavens and the earth; of these, four are sacred." (Quran 9:36)

It is an opportunity to set spiritual goals for the year ahead.
events.tasu-a:
# Tasu'a (9th Muharram)

Tasu'a is the 9th day of Muharram. It is highly recommended to fast on this day along with the 10th (Ashura).

**Virtue:**  
The Prophet (ﷺ) intended to fast on this day to distinguish the Muslim practice from others. Ibn Abbas reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

> "If I remain (alive) till the next year, I shall also fast on the ninth." (Sahih Muslim)

Fasting on the 9th prepares the soul for Ashura and ensures the Sunnah is fulfilled completely.
events.ashura:
# The Day of Ashura (10th Muharram)

Ashura is a day of great historical significance and divine mercy. It is the day Allah saved Prophet Musa (AS) and the Children of Israel from Pharaoh.

**Virtue of Fasting:**  
Fasting on Ashura expiates the sins of the previous year.

> The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Fast the Day of Ashura, for indeed I anticipate that Allah will forgive (the sins of) the year before it." (Jami` at-Tirmidhi)

It is recommended to fast on the 9th and 10th, or the 10th and 11th, to differ from previous nations.
events.mawlid:
# Mawlid al-Nabi (12th Rabi' al-Awwal)

This day marks the birth of the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), the Mercy to the Worlds.

**Significance:**  
It is a time to study his Seerah (biography), increase in sending Salawat (blessings) upon him, and emulate his noble character.

> "Indeed, Allah confers blessing upon the Prophet, and His angels [ask Him to do so]. O you who have believed, ask [ Allah to confer] blessing upon him and ask [ Allah to grant him] peace." (Quran 33:56)

Expressing love for the Prophet (ﷺ) and following his Sunnah is a core part of faith.
events.isra-miraj:
# Isra and Mi'raj (27th Rajab)

The Night Journey and Ascension is a miraculous event where the Prophet (ﷺ) traveled from Mecca to Jerusalem (Isra) and unrelated ascended to the Heavens (Mi'raj).

**Key Gifts:**  
During this journey, the five daily prayers (Salah) were ordained by Allah directly to the Prophet (ﷺ). It underscores the importance of prayer as the believer's spiritual ascension (Mi'raj).

**Recommended Acts:**  
- Increase in Salah and voluntary prayers.
- Reflecting on the significance of Masjid al-Aqsa.
- Making abundant Dua.
events.shab-e-barat:
# Shab-e-Barat (15th Sha'ban)

The Night of Mid-Sha'ban is considered a night of forgiveness and divine mercy.

**Virtues:**  
Several narrations indicate that Allah looks upon His creation on this night and forgives them, except for those who harbor intense hatred or commit shirk.

> The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah looks down on the night of the middle of Sha'ban and forgives all His creation, apart from the idolater and the mushahin (one bent on hatred)." (Sunan Ibn Majah)

It is a recommended time for seeking forgiveness (Istighfar) and visiting graveyards to pray for the deceased, as practiced by the Prophet (ﷺ).
events.ramadan-start:
# The Blessed Month of Ramadan

Ramadan is the holiest month in Islam, the month of the Quran, mercy, and forgiveness.

**Virtues:**  
- **Devils Chained:** The gates of Paradise are opened, gates of Hell are closed, and devils are chained.
- **Multiplied Rewards:** Good deeds are rewarded manifold.
- **Fasting:** Fasting is one of the pillars of Islam.

> "O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting as it was decreed upon those before you that you may become righteous." (Quran 2:183)

> The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith and expectation of reward, his previous sins will be forgiven." (Sahih Bukhari)
events.laylat-al-qadr:
# Laylat al-Qadr (The Night of Decree)

Found in the odd nights of the last ten days of Ramadan, this night is better than a thousand months of worship.

**Virtues:**  
- **Revelation:** The Quran was revealed on this night.
- **Angels:** Angels descend with peace and divine decrees.
- **Forgiveness:** Standing in prayer on this night with faith wipes away past sins.

> "Indeed, We sent the Qur'an down during the Night of Decree... The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months." (Quran 97:1-3)

**Recommended Dua:**  
"Allahumma innaka 'afuwwun tuhibbul 'afwa fa'fu 'anni" (O Allah, You are Pardoning and love to pardon, so pardon me).
events.eid-al-fitr:
# Eid al-Fitr

Eid al-Fitr marks the successful completion of Ramadan. It is a day of joy, gratitude, and unity.

**Sunnah Acts:**  
- Paying Zakat al-Fitr before the prayer.
- Eating an odd number of dates before leaving for prayer.
- Reciting the Takbirat (Allahu Akbar...).
- Praying the Eid prayer in congregation.
- Exchanging greetings and gifts.

> The Prophet (ﷺ) forbade fasting on this day.
events.arafah:
# The Day of Arafah (9th Dhul Hijjah)

This is the most important day of Hajj and the best day of the year.

**Virtue of Fasting:**  
For non-pilgrims, fasting on this day is highly recommended.

> The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Fast the Day of Arafah, for indeed I anticipate that Allah will forgive (the sins of) the year after it, and the year before it." (Jami` at-Tirmidhi)

**Best Dua:**  
The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The best supplication is the supplication on the Day of Arafah."
events.eid-al-adha:
# Eid al-Adha

Eid al-Adha (Festival of Sacrifice) commemorates the willingness of Prophet Ibrahim (AS) to sacrifice his son Ismail (AS) in obedience to Allah.

**Significance:**  
- It marks the completion of Hajj rites.
- Offering the Udhiyah (Qurbani) is a confirmed Sunnah.
- It is a day of eating, drinking, and remembering Allah.

> "It is neither their meat nor their blood that reaches Allah, but it is piety from you that reaches Him." (Quran 22:37)
events.tashreeq-1:
# Days of Tashreeq (11th-13th Dhul Hijjah)

The days following Eid al-Adha are the Days of Tashreeq. They are days of celebration and remembrance.

**Key Rulings:**  
- **Fasting is Prohibited:** The Prophet (ﷺ) designated these as days of eating and drinking.
- **Takbir:** It is recommended to recite the Takbir after every obligatory prayer until Asr on the 13th.

> The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The Days of Tashreeq are days of eating, drinking, and remembering Allah." (Sahih Muslim)
events.tashreeq-2:

events.battle-of-badr:
# Battle of Badr (17th Ramadan)

The Battle of Badr was a decisive turning point in Islamic history, where a small group of 313 Muslims defeated a powerful army of 1000 Quraysh.

**Significance:**  
Allah granted the believers a clear victory and designated this day as "Yawm al-Furqan" (The Day of Criterion).

> "And Allah had certainly already given you victory at Badr while you were few in number. Then fear Allah; perhaps you will be grateful." (Quran 3:123)

It reminds us that victory comes from Allah and is not solely dependent on numbers or material strength.
events.conquest-of-mecca:
# Conquest of Mecca (20th Ramadan)

The peaceful Conquest of Mecca (Fath Makkah) restored the Kaaba to the worship of Allah alone.

**Key Lessons:**  
- **Mercy:** Despite years of persecution, the Prophet (ﷺ) declared general amnesty for the people of Mecca, saying: "Go, for you are free."
- **Humility:** The Prophet (ﷺ) entered Mecca with his head lowered in humility to Allah, not as a conquering king.
- **Truth Prevailing:** "Truth has come, and falsehood has departed. Indeed is falsehood, [by nature], ever bound to depart." (Quran 17:81)

recurring.monday-fast:
# Monday Fast

Fasting on Mondays is a confirmed Sunnah.

**Why Monday?**
- It is the day the Prophet (ﷺ) was born.
- It is the day revelation first came to him.
- It is a day when deeds are presented to Allah.

> The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about fasting on Monday, and he said: "That is the day on which I was born and the day on which I received Revelation." (Sahih Muslim)
recurring.thursday-fast:
# Thursday Fast

Fasting on Thursdays is a Sunnah widely practiced by the Prophet (ﷺ).

**Virtue:**
Deeds are presented to Allah on Mondays and Thursdays.

> The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Deeds are presented on Monday and Thursday, and I love that my deeds be presented while I am fasting." (Jami` at-Tirmidhi)
recurring.ayyam-al-beed:
# Ayyam al-Beed (The White Days)

The 13th, 14th, and 15th of every lunar month are called 'The White Days' because the moon is full and bright.

**Reward:**
Fasting these three days every month is equivalent to fasting for the entire lifetime (because every good deed is multiplied by ten).

> The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Fasting three days of each month is fasting for a lifetime." (Sahih Bukhari)
recurring.shawwal-six:
# Six Days of Shawwal

A highly recommended Sunnah after Ramadan.

**Virtue:**
Combined with Ramadan, it completes the reward of fasting for the entire year.
- Ramadan (30 days) x 10 = 300 days.
- 6 days of Shawwal x 10 = 60 days.
- Total = 360 days (a lunar year).

> The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever fasts Ramadan then follows it with six days of Shawwal, it is as if he fasted for a lifetime." (Sahih Muslim)
recurring.dhul-hijjah-first-nine:
# The First Ten Days of Dhul Hijjah

These are the most blessed days of the year for doing good deeds.

**Recommended Acts:**
- Fasting (especially the first 9 days).
- Dhikr (Takbir, Tahmid, Tahlil).
- Charity.
- Qurbani (Sacrifice).

> The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There are no days in which righteous deeds are more beloved to Allah than these ten days." (Sahih Bukhari)
